parts.label: Early vote
why: Registered Democrats cast 41% of the 1,773,889 ballots in North Carolina so far, against 24% for the other party.
That is 1.8 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.
Statewide numbers; this weighs less for a House race.

parts.label: National tide
why: Gallup party identification moved from Republicans 48 Democrats 45 in the third quarter of 2024 to Democrats 50 Republicans 39 in the third quarter of 2026, 14 points toward the Democrats.
This district moves 0.92 points for every point the nation moves, so it feels about 12.9 points of that tide, a tailwind for Jamie Ager.

D.t: Jamie Ager leads by 6.9 in the forecast and wins 89% of simulations. The cushion is about 21,830 votes; a one point swing is about 1,580 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +0.4 and D +14.3. A normal polling error decides it.
